content: Before using vaginal metronidazole, inform your healthcare provider about all medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently taking. Specifically, disclose if you are using any of the following: Warfarin (Coumadin): A medication used to treat blood clots. Disulfiram (Antabuse): A medication used to treat alcoholism, especially if you have taken it within the past two weeks. Lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid): A medication used to treat bipolar disorder. Overdose Instructions: If you or someone else has accidentally used too much vaginal metronidazole, seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose Instructions: If you miss a dose of vaginal metronidazole, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with the next one. Do not use double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to minimize the risk of developing resistance to this medication or similar drugs. Precautions: Allergies: Do not use vaginal metronidazole if you are allergic to: Metronidazole Nuvesse Vandazole Parabens Any other nitroimidazole derivatives Any ingredients in the specific product dispensed. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients. Drug Interactions: Vaginal metronidazole may interact with other medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Avoid using vaginal metronidazole with alcohol or foods containing alcohol (e.g., propylene glycol), as this can lead to serious side effects. Refrain from consuming alcohol during treatment and for at least one day after stopping Nuvesse or three days after stopping Vandazole. Nervous System Problems: Inform your healthcare provider if you have any nervous system conditions, such as seizures or peripheral neuropathy, before using vaginal metronidazole. Pregnancy: The effects of vaginal metronidazole on pregnancy or an unborn baby are not fully known. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, discuss this with your healthcare provider to determine if this medication is appropriate for you. Breastfeeding: Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, inform your healthcare provider. You may need to pump and discard your breast milk while using this medication and for two days after completing treatment. Usage Guidelines: Use vaginal metronidazole only as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep this medication out of reach of children. Avoid sexual activity and the use of vaginal products (e.g., tampons, douches) while using vaginal metronidazole. This medication is for vaginal use only. If it comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them with cool water and contact your healthcare provider. Drug Interactions with Foods and Drinks: Do not consume alcohol or products containing propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least one day after stopping Nuvesse or three days after stopping Vandazole. Additional Notes: Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and personalized advice regarding your treatment.
